acceptance_criteria: A current health observation of a long-lived active provider does not become stale solely from lastSessionStartedAt age.
A recent session start without progress or success evidence is not labeled fresh provider readiness.
Observation age, process liveness, session lifetime, and progress age are separately serialized and tested.
Fresh successful-turn or probe evidence can contradict a headless authentication false negative only under an explicit bounded policy.
Active-but-idle, active-and-progressing, active-but-stalled, newly started, recently successful, and process-dead states have distinct deterministic dispositions.
Health and database evidence with mismatched provider, generation, or time authority cannot be combined into fresh corroboration.
Restart changes session generation but cannot manufacture provider recovery until a post-restart success or progress predicate is satisfied.
Clock skew, missing or invalid timestamps, stale observations, long idle periods, and process-identity reuse are fault-injected.
The provider-probe incident opens, downgrades, refreshes, and clears only through source-qualified evidence transitions.
Exact-byte privacy tests reject process or session identifiers, paths, commands, raw output, credentials, host or account identity, and content.

falsifier_or_remaining_gap: The finding would be falsified if observation freshness and provider progress were evaluated independently from session lifetime. Exact source execution instead rejected the long-lived active sample and accepted recent process birth without progress. Passing existing tests establish the current recently-started safeguard, not the missing four-axis contract; production incidence, idle policy, and progress thresholds remain implementation-time measurements.
impact: A healthy long-lived provider can stop contradicting a headless authentication false negative merely because it was not restarted recently, while a newly started but unproven child is overtrusted. Restart timing can therefore masquerade as provider recovery.
